entry.title: The stuff that's easy to miss when you ship a site
entry.summary: You build the site, deploy it, it loads fast, looks good, works on mobile. Done, right? Probably not. There's a bunch of stuff that's easy to forget because it doesn't break anything visibly. Your site works fine but behind the scenes things aren't set up right and you won't notice until it matters. Here are six things I kept seeing get missed: Your emails might not arrive. You're probably breaking privacy laws somewhere. Google might not be indexing all your pages. AI tools can't find you. Your analytics aren't tracking what you think. Your Open Graph tags are wrong or missing. None of this shows up as an error. Your site loads, everything looks fine. But you're leaking value in ways you can't see from the browser. I built a free tool called GradeMyWeb that checks all of this at once. You put in your URL, it runs 27 checks across email delivery, legal, analytics, search, AI readiness, and site quality, and gives you one letter grade. Takes 60 seconds, no signup. Try it: https://grademyweb.com Curious what other things you all commonly see get missed on launch. What's on your checklist that most people forget?

entry.summary: New: One stream. Now it goes everywhere you need it. Dev, staging, and prod. Real-time processing and long-term storage. No duplicate pipelines, no config drift, and no extra cost.
